issue.title: TUI Beads no-change refresh is linear in active rows: 133 ms at 8x vs the 100 ms sase-1h8 A1 ceiling
issue.description:
The TUI Beads pane's no-change refresh (cached-snapshot `previous=` path of
`load_beads_snapshot`) still costs time linear in active rows. It misses epic
sase-1h8's `abs:tui-nochange` criterion: medians are 15.6/32/64/133 ms at 1x/2x/4x/8x,
against a < 100 ms ceiling.

Proposed by phase bead sase-1h8.14 (perf gate, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #5); routed here
by the sase-1h8 land agent. sase-1h8.6 already removed the O(epics x issues) grouping
and the forced auto-refresh reloads. With an unchanged fingerprint, a tick does no store
read. The remaining cost is per active row on the no-change path. sase-1h8.14 suggests
row virtualization.

The synthetic corpus multiplies the active set with scale (561 non-closed at 1x, 4,196
at 8x), so this is active-set scaling. Root cause not yet pinned: profile the
`tui_cached` op to see whether the per-row cost is snapshot reconstruction, grouping,
or widget work. Then make the no-change path O(1) (reuse the previous snapshot object
when the fingerprint key matches) or virtualize rows. Drop `abs:tui-nochange` from the
`bead-perf-scale-gate` `--gate-allow` list when it passes. Read sase memory `tui.md`
before changing TUI hot paths.
